Required for anchorage- independent proliferation of transformed cells. During mitosis, supports the stabilization and elongation of the intracellular bridge between dividing cells. Cooperates with EXOC2 to recruit other components of the exocyst to the early midbody. During mitosis, also controls mitochondrial fission by recruiting to the mitochondrion RALBP1, which mediates the phosphorylation and activation of DNM1L by the mitotic kinase cyclin B- CDK1.

gene.name: RAN binding protein 2
gene.function: E3 SUMO-protein ligase which facilitates SUMO1 and SUMO2 conjugation by UBE2I. Involved in transport factor (Ran-GTP, karyopherin)-mediated protein import via the F-G repeat-containing domain which acts as a docking site for substrates. Binds single-stranded RNA (in vitro). May bind DNA. Component of the nuclear export pathway. Specific docking site for the nuclear export factor exportin-1. Inhibits EIF4E- dependent mRNA export. Sumoylates PML at 'Lys-490' which is essential for the proper assembly of PML-NB. Recruits BICD2 to the nuclear envelope and cytoplasmic stacks of nuclear pore complex known as annulate lamellae during G2 phase of cell cycle. Probable inactive PPIase with no peptidyl- prolyl cis-trans isomerase activity.

gene.name: ribosomal protein S6
gene.function: Component of the 40S small ribosomal subunit. Plays an important role in controlling cell growth and proliferation through the selective translation of particular classes of mRNA. Part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit. During the assembly of the SSU processome in the nucleolus, many ribosome biogenesis factors, an RNA chaperone and ribosomal proteins associate with the nascent pre-rRNA and work in concert to generate RNA folding, modifications, rearrangements and cleavage as well as targeted degradation of pre-ribosomal RNA by the RNA exosome.

gene.name: S100 calcium binding protein A9
gene.function: S100A9 is a calcium- and zinc-binding protein which plays a prominent role in the regulation of inflammatory processes and immune response. It can induce neutrophil chemotaxis, adhesion, can increase the bactericidal activity of neutrophils by promoting phagocytosis via activation of SYK, PI3K/AKT, and ERK1/2 and can induce degranulation of neutrophils by a MAPK-dependent mechanism. Predominantly found as calprotectin (S100A8/A9) which has a wide plethora of intra- and extracellular functions. The intracellular functions include: facilitating leukocyte arachidonic acid trafficking and metabolism, modulation of the tubulin-dependent cytoskeleton during migration of phagocytes and activation of the neutrophilic NADPH-oxidase. Also participates in regulatory T-cell differentiation together with CD69. Activates NADPH-oxidase by facilitating the enzyme complex assembly at the cell membrane, transferring arachidonic acid, an essential cofactor, to the enzyme complex and S100A8 contributes to the enzyme assembly by directly binding to NCF2/P67PHOX. The extracellular functions involve pro-inflammatory, antimicrobial, oxidant-scavenging and apoptosis- inducing activities. Its pro- inflammatory activity includes recruitment of leukocytes, promotion of cytokine and chemokine production, and regulation of leukocyte adhesion and migration. Acts as an alarmin or a danger associated molecular pattern (DAMP) molecule and stimulates innate immune cells via binding to pattern recognition receptors such as Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and receptor for advanced glycation endproducts (AGER). Binding to TLR4 and AGER activates the MAP-kinase and NF-kappa-B signaling pathways resulting in the amplification of the pro-inflammatory cascade. Has antimicrobial activity towards bacteria and fungi and exerts its antimicrobial activity probably via chelation of Zn(2+) which is essential for microbial growth. Can induce cell death via autophagy and apoptosis and this occurs through the cross-talk of mitochondria and lysosomes via reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the process involves BNIP3. Can regulate neutrophil number and apoptosis by an anti-apoptotic effect; regulates cell survival via ITGAM/ITGB and TLR4 and a signaling mechanism involving MEK-ERK. Its role as an oxidant scavenger has a protective role in preventing exaggerated tissue damage by scavenging oxidants. Can act as a potent amplifier of inflammation in autoimmunity as well as in cancer development and tumor spread. Has transnitrosylase activity; in oxidatively-modified low-densitity lipoprotein (LDL(ox))- induced S-nitrosylation of GAPDH on 'Cys-247' proposed to transfer the NO moiety from NOS2/iNOS to GAPDH via its own S-nitrosylated Cys-3. The iNOS-S100A8/A9 transnitrosylase complex is proposed to also direct selective inflammatory stimulus-dependent S- nitrosylation of multiple targets such as ANXA5, EZR, MSN and VIM by recognizing a [IL]-x-C-x-x-[DE] motif.

gene.name: SUMO1 activating enzyme subunit 1
gene.function: The heterodimer acts as an E1 ligase for SUMO1, SUMO2, SUMO3, and probably SUMO4. It mediates ATP-dependent activation of SUMO proteins followed by formation of a thioester bond between a SUMO protein and a conserved active site cysteine residue on UBA2/SAE2.

gene.name: sodium voltage-gated channel alpha subunit 1
gene.function: Pore-forming subunit of Nav1.1, a voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channel that directly mediates the depolarizing phase of action potentials in excitable membranes. Navs, also called VGSCs (voltage- gated sodium channels) or VDSCs (voltage-dependent sodium channels), operate by switching between closed and open conformations depending on the voltage difference across the membrane. In the open conformation they allow Na(+) ions to selectively pass through the pore, along their electrochemical gradient. The influx of Na(+) ions provokes membrane depolarization, initiating the propagation of electrical signals throughout cells and tissues. By regulating the excitability of neurons, ensures that they respond appropriately to synaptic inputs, maintaining the balance between excitation and inhibition in brain neural circuits (By similarity). Nav1.1 plays a role in controlling the excitability and action potential propagation from somatosensory neurons, thereby contributing to the sensory perception of mechanically-induced pain (By similarity). .

gene.name: semaphorin 6B
gene.function: Functions as a cell surface repellent for mossy fibers of developing neurons in the hippocampus where it plays a role in axon guidance. May function through the PLXNA4 receptor expressed by mossy cell axons. .

gene.name: SUMO specific peptidase 1
gene.function: Protease that catalyzes two essential functions in the SUMO pathway. The first is the hydrolysis of an alpha-linked peptide bond at the C-terminal end of the small ubiquitin- like modifier (SUMO) propeptides, SUMO1, SUMO2 and SUMO3 leading to the mature form of the proteins. The second is the deconjugation of SUMO1, SUMO2 and SUMO3 from targeted proteins, by cleaving an epsilon-linked peptide bond between the C-terminal glycine of the mature SUMO and the lysine epsilon-amino group of the target protein. Deconjugates SUMO1 from HIPK2. Deconjugates SUMO1 from HDAC1 and BHLHE40/DEC1, which decreases its transcriptional repression activity. Deconjugates SUMO1 from CLOCK, which decreases its transcriptional activation activity. Deconjugates SUMO2 from MTA1. Inhibits N(6)-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation by mediating SUMO1 deconjugation from METTL3 and ALKBH5: METTL3 inhibits the m6A RNA methyltransferase activity, while ALKBH5 desumoylation promotes m6A demethylation. Desumoylates CCAR2 which decreases its interaction with SIRT1. Deconjugates SUMO1 from GPS2.

gene.name: SH3 and multiple ankyrin repeat domains 3
gene.function: Major scaffold postsynaptic density protein which interacts with multiple proteins and complexes to orchestrate the dendritic spine and synapse formation, maturation and maintenance. Interconnects receptors of the postsynaptic membrane including NMDA-type and metabotropic glutamate receptors via complexes with GKAP/PSD-95 and HOMER, respectively, and the actin-based cytoskeleton. Plays a role in the structural and functional organization of the dendritic spine and synaptic junction through the interaction with Arp2/3 and WAVE1 complex as well as the promotion of the F-actin clusters. By way of this control of actin dynamics, participates in the regulation of developing neurons growth cone motility and the NMDA receptor-signaling. Also modulates GRIA1 exocytosis and GRM5/MGLUR5 expression and signaling to control the AMPA and metabotropic glutamate receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and plasticity. May be required at an early stage of synapse formation and be inhibited by IGF1 to promote synapse maturation. .

gene.name: solute carrier family 38 member 1
gene.function: Symporter that cotransports short-chain neutral amino acids and sodium ions from the extracellular to the intracellular side of the cell membrane. The transport is elctrogenic, pH dependent and driven by the Na(+) electrochemical gradient. Participates in the astroglia-derived glutamine transport into GABAergic interneurons for neurotransmitter GABA de novo synthesis (By similarity). May also contributes to amino acid transport in placental trophoblasts. Also regulates synaptic plasticity.

gene.name: solute carrier family 6 member 1
gene.function: Mediates transport of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) together with sodium and chloride and is responsible for the reuptake of GABA from the synapse. The translocation of GABA, however, may also occur in the reverse direction leading to the release of GABA (By similarity). The direction and magnitude of GABA transport is a consequence of the prevailing thermodynamic conditions, determined by membrane potential and the intracellular and extracellular concentrations of Na(+), Cl(-) and GABA (By similarity). Can also mediate sodium- and chloride-dependent transport of hypotaurine but to a much lower extent as compared to GABA (By similarity).

gene.name: SWI/SNF related BAF chromatin remodeling complex subunit B1
gene.function: Core component of the BAF (hSWI/SNF) complex. This ATP- dependent chromatin-remodeling complex plays important roles in cell proliferation and differentiation, in cellular antiviral activities and inhibition of tumor formation. The BAF complex is able to create a stable, altered form of chromatin that constrains fewer negative supercoils than normal. This change in supercoiling would be due to the conversion of up to one-half of the nucleosomes on polynucleosomal arrays into asymmetric structures, termed altosomes, each composed of 2 histones octamers. Stimulates in vitro the remodeling activity of SMARCA4/BRG1/BAF190A. Involved in activation of CSF1 promoter. Belongs to the neural progenitors-specific chromatin remodeling complex (npBAF complex) and the neuron-specific chromatin remodeling complex (nBAF complex). During neural development a switch from a stem/progenitor to a postmitotic chromatin remodeling mechanism occurs as neurons exit the cell cycle and become committed to their adult state. The transition from proliferating neural stem/progenitor cells to postmitotic neurons requires a switch in subunit composition of the npBAF and nBAF complexes. As neural progenitors exit mitosis and differentiate into neurons, npBAF complexes which contain ACTL6A/BAF53A and PHF10/BAF45A, are exchanged for homologous alternative ACTL6B/BAF53B and DPF1/BAF45B or DPF3/BAF45C subunits in neuron-specific complexes (nBAF). The npBAF complex is essential for the self-renewal/proliferative capacity of the multipotent neural stem cells. The nBAF complex along with CREST plays a role regulating the activity of genes essential for dendrite growth (By similarity). Plays a key role in cell-cycle control and causes cell cycle arrest in G0/G1.

gene.name: superoxide dismutase 1
gene.function: Destroys radicals which are normally produced within the cells and which are toxic to biological systems. Catalyzes the oxidation of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) to sulfate, playing an important role in detoxifying H2S and limiting the accumulation of reactive sulfur species (RSS) such as persulfides and polysulfides.

gene.name: small ubiquitin like modifier 1
gene.function: Ubiquitin-like protein that can be covalently attached to proteins as a monomer or a lysine-linked polymer. Covalent attachment via an isopeptide bond to its substrates requires prior activation by the E1 complex SAE1-SAE2 and linkage to the E2 enzyme UBE2I, and can be promoted by E3 ligases such as PIAS1-4, RANBP2 or CBX4. This post- translational modification on lysine residues of proteins plays a crucial role in a number of cellular processes such as nuclear transport, DNA replication and repair, mitosis and signal transduction. Involved for instance in targeting RANGAP1 to the nuclear pore complex protein RANBP2. Covalently attached to the voltage-gated potassium channel KCNB1; this modulates the gating characteristics of KCNB1. Polymeric SUMO1 chains are also susceptible to polyubiquitination which functions as a signal for proteasomal degradation of modified proteins. May also regulate a network of genes involved in palate development. Covalently attached to ZFHX3.

gene.name: synapsin II
gene.function: Neuronal phosphoprotein that coats synaptic vesicles, binds to the cytoskeleton, and is believed to function in the regulation of neurotransmitter release. May play a role in noradrenaline secretion by sympathetic neurons (By similarity). .

gene.name: transcription factor 4
gene.function: Transcription factor that binds to the immunoglobulin enhancer Mu-E5/KE5-motif. Involved in the initiation of neuronal differentiation. Activates transcription by binding to the E box (5'- CANNTG-3'). Binds to the E-box present in the somatostatin receptor 2 initiator element (SSTR2-INR) to activate transcription (By similarity). Preferentially binds to either 5'-ACANNTGT-3' or 5'- CCANNTGG-3'. .

gene.name: transformation/transcription domain associated protein
gene.function: Adapter protein, which is found in various multiprotein chromatin complexes with histone acetyltransferase activity (HAT), which gives a specific tag for epigenetic transcription activation. Component of the NuA4 histone acetyltransferase complex which is responsible for acetylation of nucleosomal histones H4 and H2A. Plays a central role in MYC transcription activation, and also participates in cell transformation by MYC. Required for p53/TP53-, E2F1- and E2F4- mediated transcription activation. Also involved in transcription activation mediated by the adenovirus E1A, a viral oncoprotein that deregulates transcription of key genes. Probably acts by linking transcription factors such as E1A, MYC or E2F1 to HAT complexes such as STAGA thereby allowing transcription activation. Probably not required in the steps following histone acetylation in processes of transcription activation. May be required for the mitotic checkpoint and normal cell cycle progression. Component of a SWR1-like complex that specifically mediates the removal of histone H2A.Z/H2AZ1 from the nucleosome. May play a role in the formation and maintenance of the auditory system (By similarity).

gene.name: ubiquitin conjugating enzyme E2 E3
gene.function: Accepts ubiquitin from the E1 complex and catalyzes its covalent attachment to other proteins. In vitro catalyzes 'Lys-11'- and 'Lys-48'-, as well as 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitination. Participates in the regulation of transepithelial sodium transport in renal cells.

gene.name: ubiquinol-cytochrome c reductase complex III subunit VII
gene.function: Component of the ubiquinol-cytochrome c oxidoreductase, a multisubunit transmembrane complex that is part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain which drives oxidative phosphorylation. The respiratory chain contains 3 multisubunit complexes succinate dehydrogenase (complex II, CII), ubiquinol-cytochrome c oxidoreductase (cytochrome b-c1 complex, complex III, CIII) and cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV, CIV), that cooperate to transfer electrons derived from NADH and succinate to molecular oxygen, creating an electrochemical gradient over the inner membrane that drives transmembrane transport and the ATP synthase. The cytochrome b-c1 complex catalyzes electron transfer from ubiquinol to cytochrome c, linking this redox reaction to translocation of protons across the mitochondrial inner membrane, with protons being carried across the membrane as hydrogens on the quinol. In the process called Q cycle, 2 protons are consumed from the matrix, 4 protons are released into the intermembrane space and 2 electrons are passed to cytochrome c. .

gene.name: zinc finger protein 620
gene.function: May be involved in transcriptional regulation.

phenotype.definition: A state of excessive motor activity that is associated with mental distress or a feeling of substantial unease or inner tension. Distinguished from restlessness by the increased level of emotional distress and negative intensity of the experience. Agitation has a significant level of physical activity that is typically threatening to the self or others.

Intense feelings of nervousness, tension, or panic often arise in response to interpersonal stresses. There is worry about the negative effects of past unpleasant experiences and future negative possibilities. Individuals may feel fearful, apprehensive, or threatened by uncertainty, and they may also have fears of falling apart or losing control.
Lack of breathing with no movement of the respiratory muscles and no exchange of air in the lungs. This term refers to a disposition to have recurrent episodes of apnea rather than to a single event.

A benign paroxysmal nonepileptic disorder occurring in healthy children 6 to 48 months of age. The episodes start with a provocation such as emotional upset or minor injury, and might progress to breath holding, cyanosis, and syncope.
Abnormal cognition is characterized by deficits in thinking, reasoning, or remembering.
Infrequent or difficult evacuation of feces.
Loss of developmental skills, as manifested by loss of developmental milestones.
Abnormally increased frequency (usually defined as three or more) loose or watery bowel movements a day.
Impaired ability to eat related to problems gathering food and getting ready to suck, chew, or swallow it.
Abnormal intestinal contractions, such as spasms and intestinal paralysis, related to the loss of the ability of the gut to coordinate muscular activity because of endogenous or exogenous causes.

Hyperventilation refers to an increased pulmonary ventilation rate that is faster than necessary for the exchange of gases. Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). papers.title: Trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome: a randomized phase 3 study.
papers.summary: The LAVENDER phase 3 study found that 12 weeks of twice-daily trofinetide significantly improved Rett syndrome behavioral symptoms, clinician-rated improvement, and caregiver-rated social communication compared with placebo. Benefit was medium in effect size, but diarrhea and vomiting were frequent treatment-emergent adverse events and caused most discontinuations.
papers.why: This randomized phase 3 trial provides direct evidence that trofinetide improves core Rett symptoms using validated clinical and communication outcome measures.

papers.title: The new big is small: Leveraging knowledge from small trials for rare disease drug development: Blarcamesine for Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper's model-informed reanalysis of two small trials found that low-dose blarcamesine reduced neurobehavioral symptoms and latent Rett syndrome severity, with stronger responses reported in participants carrying common wild-type SIGMAR1 rs- genotypes. Pharmacometrics item response theory modelling, population pharmacokinetics, Bayes factors, and subgroup analyses provided efficacy and evidence-strength estimates, but the short duration and design did not establish a disease-modifying effect.
papers.why: Applies item response theory and Bayesian analysis to a small blarcamesine trial in Rett syndrome, providing a reusable method for extracting efficacy evidence from limited rare-disease trials.

papers.title: Efficacy and tolerance of cannabidiol in the treatment of epilepsy in patients with Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: In a small retrospective cohort of 10 girls with genetically confirmed Rett syndrome and pharmacoresistant epilepsy, adjunctive cannabidiol reduced seizure frequency in 70% and was generally well tolerated, with additional caregiver-reported reductions in agitation or anxiety and improvement in spasticity. Cannabidiol did not change measured Rett syndrome severity or EEG findings and enabled no reduction of the antiseizure-medication regimen; prior preclinical and atypical Rett syndrome evidence provides additional but non-contemporaneous support for cannabinoid use.
papers.why: Reports real-world use of cannabidiol in Rett syndrome-associated epilepsy, including seizure reduction, tolerability, and behavioral or spasticity outcomes.

papers.title: Randomized open-label trial of dextromethorphan in Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: In a prospective randomized open-label trial, dextromethorphan was safe in 35 girls aged 3–15 years with Rett syndrome and showed dose-dependent improvements in clinical seizures, receptive language, and behavioral hyperactivity. Global clinical severity and EEG spike counts did not improve significantly, although limited precision prevented exclusion of an important effect on EEG spikes.
papers.why: A randomized open-label trial directly tested dextromethorphan in girls with Rett syndrome and quantified seizure, behavioral, cognitive, EEG, and global-severity outcomes.

papers.title: Fenfluramine in Rett syndrome: A multidimensional clinical study.
papers.summary: In a prospective, uncontrolled study of eight children with classic Rett syndrome carrying pathogenic MECP2 variants and drug-resistant epilepsy, adjunctive fenfluramine was associated with improvements in seizures and several nonseizure domains, including behavior, sleep, breathing, motor function, and clinical severity. The findings support further controlled evaluation, but causality and generalizability are limited by the small, single-center, single-arm design, and respiratory outcomes were assessed with clinical scales rather than objective respiratory measurements.
papers.why: This prospective Rett syndrome study reports seizure, behavioral, sleep, respiratory, motor, quality-of-life, and neurophysiological outcomes associated with adjunctive fenfluramine.

papers.title: Pharmacological treatment with mirtazapine rescues cortical atrophy and respiratory deficits in MeCP2 null mice.
papers.summary: In MeCP2−/y mice, two weeks of mirtazapine partially restored brain and somatosensory-cortical abnormalities and fully or substantially rescued dendritic morphology, spine defects, heart and breath rates, anxiety-related behavior, and GABAergic and glutamatergic responses in cortex and brainstem. Mirtazapine did not rescue body weight, did not improve hippocampal layer thickness, and did not significantly improve oxygen saturation, while desipramine was less effective for several functional outcomes and reduced some cardiovascular measures.
papers.why: Mirtazapine rescued cortical atrophy, dendritic and spine abnormalities, cardiorespiratory deficits, behavior, and neurochemical abnormalities in MeCP2-null mice.

papers.title: Pharmacologic Treatment of Rett Syndrome With Glatiramer Acetate.
papers.summary: A prospective, open-label phase II trial found preliminary evidence that glatiramer acetate improved gait velocity, memory, and the breath-holding index in 10 ambulatory girls with genetically confirmed Rett syndrome; epileptiform discharges decreased in the four patients who had them at baseline. Quality of life showed a nonsignificant improvement trend, and the small uncontrolled study supports larger controlled trials rather than establishing efficacy.
papers.why: An open-label phase II trial in patients with Rett syndrome found preliminary improvements in gait, memory, breath holding, and epileptiform discharges with glatiramer acetate.

papers.title: Autistic-like social deficits in hippocampal MeCP2 knockdown rat models are rescued by ketamine.
papers.summary: The paper shows that hippocampal MECP2 knockdown in rats produces anxiety, repetitive behavior, and autistic-like social deficits, while a single 20 mg/kg ketamine injection acutely restores several social-interaction measures. Ketamine also increases hippocampal Glur1/PSD-95-related expression in the knockdown model, but these molecular changes were not established as the mechanism of behavioral rescue and do not demonstrate efficacy in people with Rett syndrome.
papers.why: The study provides a MeCP2-related rat model and direct evidence that a single ketamine treatment rescues autism-associated social deficits caused by hippocampal MeCP2 knockdown.

papers.title: An Update on Psychopharmacological Treatment of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.summary: This review reports that trofinetide at 200 mg/kg/day significantly improved several behavioral and clinician-rated outcomes in a controlled phase 2 trial of 82 children with Rett syndrome. It also reports that the sigma-1 receptor agonist blarcamesine rescued behavior and brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in a Rett syndrome mouse model, with efficacy additionally claimed from a controlled patient trial.
papers.why: Although focused on autism, the review identifies tested pharmacological and nutritional approaches plus a genetic-disorder treatment model that may transfer to overlapping Rett phenotypes.

papers.title: Dysfunction in GABA signalling mediates autism-like stereotypies and Rett syndrome phenotypes.
papers.summary: Conditional MeCP2 deletion from GABAergic neurons in mice reproduced many Rett syndrome phenotypes, including stereotypies, motor dysfunction, respiratory abnormalities, and premature lethality. Mechanistically, neuronal MeCP2 loss reduced Gad1/Gad2 expression, intracellular GABA, inhibitory quantal size, and GABA release, while more restricted forebrain deletion produced behavioral abnormalities without respiratory dysfunction, seizures, or EEG hyperexcitability.
papers.why: Conditional MeCP2-deficient mice reproduce Rett and autism-related motor stereotypies, while electrophysiology and molecular measurements identify deficient GABAergic signaling as a testable disease mechanism.

papers.title: Efficient derivation of microglia-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells.
papers.summary: The study establishes a serum-free protocol for differentiating human embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells into microglia-like cells and integrating them into three-dimensional neural cultures. Isogenic MECP2-mutant cells generated smaller pMGLs than wild-type controls, providing a human cellular model for investigating Rett syndrome-associated microglial phenotypes.
papers.why: This efficient differentiation system generates Rett iPSC-derived microglia-like cells and supports their study in a tissue-like 3D environment, enabling disease-relevant modeling.

papers.title: Disruption of DNA-methylation-dependent long gene repression in Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: This paper shows that loss or disruption of MeCP2 causes a length-dependent up-regulation of long, neuronal-enriched genes, with repression depending strongly on mCA methylation within gene bodies. In cultured cortical neurons, topotecan partially reverses the excess long-gene expression and improves the reduced cellular rRNA content caused by MeCP2 knockdown, suggesting rebalancing long-gene expression as a potential therapeutic strategy.
papers.why: Reducing abnormally elevated long-gene expression attenuated cellular deficits in MeCP2-deficient neurons, providing an experimentally supported therapeutic strategy and mechanistic readout.

papers.title: L1 retrotransposition in neurons is modulated by MeCP2.
papers.summary: The paper shows that MeCP2 restrains LINE-1 (L1) promoter activity and neuronal retrotransposition, with increased L1 activity observed after MeCP2 loss in mouse models, Rett syndrome patient-derived neural progenitor cells, and postmortem Rett syndrome brain tissue. MeCP2 complementation reduces the reporter-positive fraction in patient-derived cells, although the authors cannot determine whether increased retrotransposition contributes causally to Rett syndrome pathology or is a consequence of disease.
papers.why: Demonstrates increased L1 retrotransposition in MeCP2-deficient human neuronal progenitor cells and tissues from people with Rett syndrome, supporting a disease-relevant molecular assay or biomarker.

papers.title: Wild-type microglia arrest pathology in a mouse model of Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: Wild-type bone marrow engrafted MECP2-expressing microglia into the brains of Mecp2-null male mice and arrested multiple facets of Rett syndrome pathology, while peripheral immune reconstitution alone or late, weak engraftment was insufficient. Myeloid-cell Mecp2 expression produced similar benefits, and pharmacological blockade of phagocytic engulfment abolished the rescue, implicating microglial phagocytic activity as a major mechanistic component.
papers.why: Shows in a Mecp2-null mouse model that wild-type microglial engraftment or myeloid MECP2 expression arrests multiple Rett-like pathologies and identifies a potential bone-marrow transplantation strategy.

papers.title: Exosomes regulate neurogenesis and circuit assembly.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The paper shows that neural exosomes promote neurogenesis, synaptogenesis, and neural-network activity, and that exosomes from isogenic MECP2-corrected control cultures rescue several developmental deficits in human MECP2 loss-of-function neural models. MECP2 loss of function also alters exosome protein cargo and removes much of the exosome bioactivity needed to promote neuronal development, while MECP2LOF exosomes do not acutely worsen control cultures.
papers.why: Exosomes from isogenic control neural cultures rescued proliferation, differentiation, synaptogenesis, and synchronized-firing deficits in MECP2-deficient neural cultures.

papers.title: MeCP2-regulated miRNAs control early human neurogenesis through differential effects on ERK and AKT signaling.
papers.summary: MeCP2 deficiency in Rett syndrome patient-derived and knockdown neuronal models increased miR-199 and miR-214, altered PAK4–ERK and PTEN–AKT signaling, and impaired early neuronal differentiation and migration. Inhibiting either miRNA partially restored target proteins, signaling, and neuronal differentiation, while either miRNA overexpression disrupted prenatal mouse neurogenesis and migration.
papers.why: Uses Rett-specific iPSC, knockdown, and organoid systems to show that inhibiting two MeCP2-regulated miRNAs restores ERK/AKT signaling and rescues neuronal differentiation abnormalities.

papers.title: CDKL5 ensures excitatory synapse stability by reinforcing NGL-1-PSD95 interaction in the postsynaptic compartment and is impaired in patient iPSC-derived neurons.
papers.summary: The paper shows that CDKL5 phosphorylates the synaptic cell-adhesion molecule NGL-1 at S631, thereby strengthening NGL-1 binding to PSD95 and maintaining excitatory synapses and dendritic-spine morphology. CDKL5-deficient mouse neurons and patient iPSC-derived neurons from individuals with atypical Rett syndrome exhibited synaptic defects, while a phosphomimetic NGL-1 S631E mutant partially rescued spine morphology but not spine number.
papers.why: The paper develops patient-derived neuronal models and experimentally demonstrates rescue of CDKL5-associated synaptic defects by enhancing NGL-1–PSD95 binding.

papers.title: Rett syndrome mutation MeCP2 T158A disrupts DNA binding, protein stability and ERP responses.
papers.summary: The paper establishes that the MECP2 T158A mutation is a partial loss-of-function mutation that causes Rett syndrome-like neurobehavioral abnormalities in a knock-in mouse by reducing MeCP2 protein stability and binding to methylated DNA. Auditory event-related potentials and time-frequency EEG measures showed age-dependent abnormalities and were proposed as potential biomarkers for Rett syndrome phenotypes and treatment evaluation, but no therapeutic intervention was directly tested.
papers.why: The study develops a mutation-specific Rett mouse model and provides data supporting event-related potentials as biomarkers and treatment-evaluation endpoints.

papers.title: High frequency of mosaic pathogenic variants in genes causing epilepsy-related neurodevelopmental disorders.
papers.summary: High-read-depth next-generation sequencing identified a mosaic MECP2 pathogenic variant in a male with atypical Rett syndrome and also detected parental MECP2 mosaicism. The study supports repeat next-generation sequencing and quantitative parental testing because these methods are more sensitive than conventional Sanger sequencing for detecting low-level mosaicism.
papers.why: The study validates next-generation sequencing approaches for detecting low-level somatic and parental mosaic pathogenic variants in MECP2 and related genes.

papers.title: Characterization of human mosaic Rett syndrome brain tissue by single-nucleus RNA sequencing.
papers.summary: The paper establishes single-cell and single-nucleus SNP sequencing as a way to assign mutant or wild-type X-chromosome transcriptotypes and compare gene expression within the same mosaic brain. In human Rett syndrome cortex and mouse models, the data show that loss of MECP2 causes a conserved, cell-autonomous failure to repress highly methylated long genes, particularly in excitatory neurons, while also identifying indirect gene-expression effects in wild-type neurons from mosaic females.
papers.why: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing resolves mutant and wild-type cells in human and mouse Rett brain tissue and identifies cell-type-specific methylation-associated expression changes.

papers.title: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of trofinetide in pediatric Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: This phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled pediatric trial found that trofinetide was generally safe and well tolerated at 50, 100, and 200 mg/kg twice daily in children and adolescents with Rett syndrome. At 200 mg/kg twice daily, trofinetide significantly improved three core efficacy measures—RSBQ total score, CGI-I, and RTT-DSC-VAS—relative to placebo, with exploratory evidence of exposure-response correlations; however, the cohort was small, treatment duration was short, multiplicity was not adjusted, and no validated biomarkers predicted response.
papers.why: A phase 2 randomized controlled trial directly demonstrates trofinetide tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and improvement on Rett syndrome clinical outcome measures in children and adolescents.

papers.title: Mecp2-null mice provide new neuronal targets for Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: The study compared wild-type and Mecp2-null mouse brains and identified ten genes consistently upregulated after Mecp2 disruption. Chromatin immunoprecipitation classified seven as direct MeCP2 targets, two as indirectly affected, and Dlk1 as indirectly affected through an upstream Gtl2 regulatory region; DNA methylation did not differ between wild-type and knockout brains.
papers.why: This study directly uses Mecp2-null mice and experimentally validated molecular assays to identify Rett syndrome disease mechanisms and candidate therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Rett-causing mutations reveal two domains critical for MeCP2 function and for toxicity in MECP2 duplication syndrome mice.
papers.summary: Transgenic mice carrying the Rett-associated MECP2 R111G or R306C mutations model distinct severities of Rett syndrome and show that both the methyl-CpG binding domain and transcriptional repression domain must be functional for MeCP2 duplication toxicity. R111G abolishes methyl-CpG binding and produces a null-like phenotype, whereas R306C retains methyl-CpG binding but disrupts NCoR-complex interactions and reduces DNA binding through the C-terminal basic cluster, producing a milder but progressive Rett phenotype.
papers.why: This study directly models Rett-causing MECP2 mutations and identifies functional domains that drive Rett phenotypes and MeCP2 toxicity, providing reusable disease models and mechanistic assays.

papers.title: Pharmacological reversal of synaptic and network pathology in human MECP2-KO neurons and cortical organoids.
papers.summary: In human MECP2-knockout neurons, mosaic neurospheres, and cortical organoids modeling Rett syndrome, Nefiracetam and PHA 543613 partially reversed defects in synaptic expression, calcium activity, and network spiking while generally leaving controls unaffected. The treatments did not fully restore all phenotypes, and this preclinical study did not test efficacy in patients with Rett syndrome.
papers.why: The study uses Rett-relevant human neuronal and organoid models to screen compounds and reports reversal of MECP2-associated synaptic and network pathology with two lead drugs.

papers.title: Consensus guidelines on managing Rett syndrome across the lifespan.
papers.summary: This consensus guideline describes Rett syndrome as a MECP2-associated, multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder and provides age-dependent surveillance and management recommendations. It highlights treatable complications—including gastrointestinal disease, seizures, prolonged QTc, scoliosis, nutritional impairment and osteoporosis—while emphasizing that specific therapies remain insufficiently tested and that some outcomes and prognostic features remain uncertain.
papers.why: This consensus guideline provides a reusable clinical care and monitoring framework for managing Rett syndrome and its multisystem comorbidities across the lifespan.

papers.title: The molecular basis of variable phenotypic severity among common missense mutations causing Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: This study establishes three knock-in mouse models for common MECP2 missense variants associated with Rett syndrome and shows that their molecular and behavioral severity mirrors human disease severity. T158M and R133C reduce MeCP2 abundance and chromatin/DNA binding, with T158M producing the more severe molecular defect, whereas R306C primarily affects NCoR/SMRT-related function with relatively preserved MeCP2 abundance and DNA binding.
papers.why: This paper reports a validated allelic mouse series reproducing the severity spectrum of common Rett missense mutations and provides mutation-specific molecular readouts for therapy development.

papers.title: MeCP2 modulates gene expression pathways in astrocytes.
papers.summary: Integrated expression microarray and MeCP2 ChIP-seq analyses identified a set of genes whose expression or MeCP2 binding changes in MeCP2-deficient mouse cortical astrocytes. Validation supported altered expression of Apoc2, Cdon, Csrp, and Nrep and suggested that disrupted astrocytic signaling, cell division, neuronal support, and glutamate-pathway genes may contribute to Rett syndrome phenotypes.
papers.why: The study establishes an integrated molecular screening method and identifies validated astrocyte MeCP2-responsive genes relevant to Rett syndrome mechanisms.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic spectral power as a marker of cortical function and disease severity in girls with Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 57 girls with Rett syndrome and 37 typically developing controls, resting-state EEG revealed regionally reduced alpha/beta power, increased relative delta power, and a more negative power-spectrum slope. Increased frontal delta or theta power and a more negative slope were associated with poorer performance on cognitive assessments, supporting EEG spectral measures as candidate markers of cortical dysfunction and disease severity, although longitudinal validation is required.
papers.why: The study identifies reproducible EEG power and spectral-slope differences in Rett syndrome and associations with cognitive impairment, supporting candidate severity biomarkers.

papers.title: Dysregulation of the long non-coding RNA transcriptome in a Rett syndrome mouse model.
papers.summary: This paper shows that loss of Mecp2 in a Rett syndrome mouse model causes broad dysregulation of brain long non-coding RNAs, with 701 lncRNAs significantly altered. The study particularly links Mecp2-dependent regulation of AK081227 and AK087060 to altered expression of their host genes, with AK081227 upregulation associated with Gabrr2 downregulation across four brain regions.
papers.why: The study profiles disease-associated lncRNA changes in Mecp2-null mouse brain and experimentally links two lncRNAs to altered neuronal gene expression.

papers.title: Lack of Cdkl5 Disrupts the Organization of Excitatory and Inhibitory Synapses and Parvalbumin Interneurons in the Primary Visual Cortex.
papers.summary: In Cdkl5−/y mice modeling the Hanefeld variant of Rett syndrome, the paper demonstrates reduced cortical activity and selective disruption of excitatory synapses, parvalbumin interneurons, and perineuronal-net maturation in the primary visual cortex. These abnormalities provide an anatomical basis for the disorder’s visual deficits and support a shared excitation/inhibition mechanism across Rett syndrome variants.
papers.why: CDKL5-null mice reproduce human CDKL5-related Rett syndrome features and provide experimentally validated cellular and synaptic readouts of visual-circuit dysfunction.

papers.title: MECP2 isoform-specific vectors with regulated expression for Rett syndrome gene therapy.
papers.summary: This paper develops self-inactivating retroviral and insulated lentiviral vectors that express the MECP2 E1 or E2 isoforms in murine neural stem cells and neurons, with the MeP promoter reproducing the endogenous neuron-and-glia expression pattern while avoiding substantial undifferentiated NSC expression. In an ex vivo Mecp2tm1.1Bird+/− Rett syndrome model, the vectors restored MECP2 expression in 95–100% of differentiated cells, and MECP2-E1 expression increased dendritic length and branching, but no in vivo clinical efficacy was established.
papers.why: The study develops MECP2 gene-transfer vectors that restore MeCP2 expression and improve neuronal dendritic branching in an ex vivo Rett syndrome model.

papers.title: MeCP2 SUMOylation rescues Mecp2-mutant-induced behavioural deficits in a mouse model of Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: The study identifies PIAS1-dependent MeCP2 SUMOylation at Lys-412 as a neuronal-activity-regulated mechanism that releases CREB, increases BDNF expression, and supports social novelty, fear memory, and hippocampal long-term potentiation. Wild-type or SUMO-modified MeCP2, but not SUMOylation-defective MeCP2K412R, rescued major behavioral and electrophysiological deficits in Mecp2 conditional-knockout mice, while acute IGF-1 or CRF treatment increased MeCP2 SUMOylation in rat hippocampus.
papers.why: The study mechanistically identifies impaired MeCP2 SUMOylation in Rett neurons and demonstrates rescue of behavioral and synaptic deficits by modified MeCP2 re-expression in a disease model.

papers.title: Cytokine Dysregulation in MECP2- and CDKL5-Related Rett Syndrome: Relationships with Aberrant Redox Homeostasis, Inflammation, and ω-3 PUFAs.
papers.summary: This clinical study shows that MECP2-related and CDKL5-related Rett syndrome have distinct subclinical cytokine dysregulation, abnormal redox homeostasis, and different relationships to inflammatory status and clinical severity. Twelve months of high-dose fish-oil omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids partially counterbalanced cytokine abnormalities, oxidative-stress markers, and clinical severity in both groups, but responses were not uniform.
papers.why: The study directly tested omega-3 PUFA supplementation in MECP2- and CDKL5-related Rett syndrome and reported partial improvement in cytokine dysregulation, oxidative stress, and inflammatory status.

papers.title: Mapping pathological phenotypes in a mouse model of CDKL5 disorder.
papers.summary: Cdkl5 knockout mice model several features of CDKL5 disorder and partially overlap with Mecp2 knockout models of Rett syndrome, including hind-limb clasping, hypoactivity, reduced cortical dendritic arborization, and reduced Akt/rpS6 signaling. Cell-specific Cdkl5 deletion maps limb clasping and visual tracking deficits to glutamatergic neurons and hypolocomotion to GABAergic forebrain neurons, while spontaneous seizures are not reproduced.
papers.why: The CDKL5 knockout model reproduces Rett-like motor phenotypes and provides cellular, neurophysiological, behavioral, and molecular assays directly relevant to an associated gene in Rett syndrome.

papers.title: Developmental loss of MeCP2 from VIP interneurons impairs cortical function and behavior.
papers.summary: Conditional Mecp2 deletion in mouse VIP interneurons reproduces several neural and behavioral features of the Mecp2 loss-of-function model of Rett syndrome, including reduced cortical gamma activity, increased pyramidal-neuron firing, impaired state-dependent modulation, marble-burying deficits, and reversed social preference. VIP-specific deletion did not significantly increase mortality, alter seizure incidence, or impair open-field locomotion or elevated-plus-maze anxiety behavior, indicating a selective rather than comprehensive Rett-like phenotype.
papers.why: The conditional mouse model isolates MeCP2 loss in VIP interneurons and reproduces key neural and behavioral phenotypes of Rett syndrome.

papers.title: Whole exome sequencing of Rett syndrome-like patients reveals the mutational diversity of the clinical phenotype.
papers.summary: Whole exome sequencing of 21 female probands clinically resembling Rett syndrome but lacking MECP2, CDKL5, and FOXG1 variants identified coding de novo variants in 14 patients, revealing substantial genetic heterogeneity and reassigning some cases to other neurodevelopmental disorders. Functional testing in Caenorhabditis elegans showed locomotion defects for five of six orthologous-gene mutants, supporting the neurological relevance of several newly proposed genes while GABBR2 showed a null result in the single-mutant assay.
papers.why: Whole-exome sequencing and functional validation in C. elegans resolved Rett-like phenotypes and identified additional candidate genes with observable neurological defects.

papers.title: Enrichment of mutations in chromatin regulators in people with Rett syndrome lacking mutations in MECP2.
papers.summary: In 22 people with Rett syndrome lacking apparent MECP2, CDKL5, or FOXG1 mutations, combined whole-exome sequencing and copy-number-variant analysis identified likely causal variants in 17 of 19 cases remaining after MECP2 resequencing. The findings support heterogeneous, high-mutation-burden Rett syndrome and implicate dysregulated chromatin regulation and excitatory glutamatergic signaling as shared pathological mechanisms.
papers.why: The study demonstrates a combined sequencing and CNV workflow that identifies causal variants in a substantial fraction of genetically unresolved Rett cases.

papers.title: Neuronal non-CG methylation is an essential target for MeCP2 function.
papers.summary: The paper shows that MeCP2 binding to neuronal mCAC sites, rather than mCG binding alone, is essential for normal brain function: an MM2-EGFP knock-in mouse that retains mCG binding but cannot read mCAC or mCAT develops severe Rett-like neurological and behavioral phenotypes. Loss of mCAC-dependent transcriptional repression dysregulates highly methylated genes, including a shared set enriched for neurological disease, although the individual causal genes and therapeutic targets remain untested.
papers.why: The engineered MeCP2 domain-swap mouse directly tests non-CG methylation recognition and produces Rett-like phenotypes, clarifying an essential MeCP2 mechanism.

papers.title: Genes related to mitochondrial functions, protein degradation, and chromatin folding are differentially expressed in lymphomonocytes of Rett syndrome patients.
papers.summary: Patient peripheral blood mononuclear cells showed broad transcriptomic dysregulation in Rett syndrome, with increased expression of genes related to mitochondrial activity, ATP synthesis, redox defense, protein ubiquitination, and proteasomal degradation, alongside reduced expression of several chromatin-related genes. RT-qPCR confirmed selected changes, but the study could not determine whether ATP concentrations were increased or whether mitochondrial alterations were primary or secondary to Rett syndrome clinical features.
papers.why: This study provides patient-derived Rett syndrome expression data and identifies candidate pathway and biomarker signatures in peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

papers.title: Validating the Rett Syndrome Gross Motor Scale.
papers.summary: The Rett Syndrome Gross Motor Scale showed strong internal consistency, excellent clinical repeatability, and moderate-to-good agreement between observed and parent-reported motor skills. Gross motor performance generally declined with age, while the p.Arg133Cys, p.Arg294*, and p.Arg306Cys variants were associated with better scores than a large MECP2 deletion.
papers.why: This study validates the Rett Syndrome Gross Motor Scale for clinical practice and trials using video, parent reports, and repeated clinical assessments.

papers.title: Top caregiver concerns in Rett syndrome and related disorders: data from the US natural history study.
papers.summary: In 925 participants from the US Rett syndrome and RTT-related disorders Natural History Study, caregiver-ranked concerns most strongly identified effective communication, seizures, hand use, walking/balance, and constipation as priority clinical issues in classic Rett syndrome. The findings support caregiver-informed, multidomain clinical-trial outcome measures and show that concern profiles vary with age, clinical severity, MECP2 mutation, and diagnostic category.
papers.why: A large natural-history cohort identifies prioritized Rett syndrome concerns that can guide selection of clinically meaningful trial outcome measures.

papers.title: Advanced genetic therapies for the treatment of Rett syndrome: state of the art and future perspectives.
papers.summary: This review reports that gene replacement, targeted RNA editing, X-chromosome reactivation, and other genetic strategies can restore MECP2 function and improve Rett syndrome phenotypes in cellular or animal models, although dosage toxicity, limited brain transduction, immune responses, and incomplete rescue remain major constraints. It identifies AAV-MECP2 programs NGN-401 and TSHA-102 as clinical-stage approaches and reports that trofinetide improved clinical endpoints in a completed phase 3 trial, while CRISPR-Cas9 correction, read-through therapy, suppressor tRNA therapy, and nanoparticle delivery remain earlier-stage approaches.
papers.why: Directly reviews advanced genetic interventions for Rett syndrome, including approaches already entering clinical trials and multiple mechanisms for restoring MECP2 function.

papers.title: Subclinical inflammatory status in Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: In 25 girls with stage II Rett syndrome carrying four MECP2 mutation classes, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and mutation-severity-associated plasma proteomic changes supported the presence of a subclinical chronic inflammatory state. C-reactive protein was unchanged, while positive acute-phase proteins were generally increased and several negative acute-phase or lipid-metabolism proteins were decreased, although some proteins showed variant-dependent or mixed patterns.
papers.why: This Rett syndrome study identifies measurable inflammatory and proteomic abnormalities, including elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, that could support biomarker development and disease monitoring.

papers.title: Loss of MeCP2 in the rat models regression, impaired sociability and transcriptional deficits of Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper establishes the Mecp2 ZFN rat as a complementary model of Rett syndrome that reproduces loss of MeCP2 protein, psychomotor regression, selective sociability and play deficits, and altered fear memory. Cross-species rat, mouse, and human post-mortem transcriptomic comparisons suggest that combining rodent datasets can improve prediction of transcriptional alterations in the RTT brain, although the validation samples and gene panel were limited.
papers.why: The study validates a Mecp2-deficient rat model with psychomotor regression and juvenile-play deficits that provide complementary preclinical outcomes for Rett syndrome.

papers.title: A BDNF loop-domain mimetic acutely reverses spontaneous apneas and respiratory abnormalities during behavioral arousal in a mouse model of Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: In Mecp2-null and Mecp2-heterozygous mouse models, acute systemic LM22A-4 reduced nucleus tractus solitarius synaptic hyperexcitability, eliminated spontaneous apneas, and normalized respiratory responses to auditory arousal. The effects were not detectable in wild-type controls, were absent 24 hours later, and were not accompanied by measurable sedation-related behavioral changes.
papers.why: LM22A-4 acutely eliminated apneas and reversed respiratory dysregulation during arousal in Mecp2-mutant mice through BDNF/TrkB-related mechanisms.

papers.title: Targeted manipulation of heterochromatin rescues MeCP2 Rett mutants and re-establishes higher order chromatin organization.
papers.summary: The study shows that artificial tethering of MeCP2 Rett mutants to pericentric heterochromatin rescues the clustering defects of the R133L and R111G variants, whereas P101H, P152R, and F155S retain independent aggregation defects. The GBP-MaSat and tamoxifen-controlled GBP-ER-NLS-MaSat systems provide in-vitro tools for measuring and temporally manipulating MeCP2-dependent chromocenter clustering in C2C12 mouse myoblasts.
papers.why: The study directly demonstrates a targeted strategy that restores higher-order chromatin organization and functional activity to chromatin-binding-deficient MeCP2 Rett mutants.

papers.title: Autonomic breathing abnormalities in Rett syndrome: caregiver perspectives in an international database study.
papers.summary: This international caregiver-reported study found that breath-holding, hyperventilation, and abdominal bloating are common, burdensome autonomic disturbances in Rett syndrome, with age-related differences in prevalence and frequency. Treatment evidence was limited to very small caregiver-reported series, but improvement was consistently perceived with topiramate and acetazolamide and in treated individuals receiving CPAP/BIPAP, supporting further controlled investigation.
papers.why: The study characterizes breathing abnormalities in a large Rett cohort and proposes concrete clinical outcome measures and management approaches for trial design and care.

papers.title: MeCP2 and histone deacetylases 1 and 2 in dorsal striatum collectively suppress repetitive behaviors.
papers.summary: Conditional MeCP2 deletion in mouse forebrain reduced striatal SAPAP3 expression and increased excessive grooming, while dorsal-striatal SAPAP3 restoration rescued grooming without correcting the rotarod deficit. The study further showed that HDAC1 and HDAC2 redundantly support neuronal survival and jointly regulate SAPAP3 and repetitive grooming, suggesting a striatal mechanism transferable to repetitive behaviors in Rett syndrome.
papers.why: Using a Mecp2-deficient mouse model of Rett-related repetitive behavior, the study demonstrates that restoring striatal Sapap3 expression rescues excessive grooming and identifies a mechanistically actionable pathway.

papers.title: Clinical features and gene mutational spectrum of CDKL5-related diseases in a cohort of Chinese patients.
papers.summary: In a Chinese cohort of 102 patients, de novo CDKL5 mutations were identified in 7 of 9 girls with Hanefeld variant Rett syndrome, 2 girls with early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, and 1 boy with infantile spasms. Female carriers consistently showed early refractory seizures, severe developmental delay, and Rett-like hand stereotypies, but the small cohort did not establish a genotype–phenotype relationship or an association with X-chromosome inactivation pattern.
papers.why: The cohort study provides a practical diagnostic strategy for identifying CDKL5-related Rett/Hanefeld variants in patients with Rett-like phenotypes or unexplained early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.

papers.title: Evidence-Based Physical Therapy for Individuals with Rett Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review found 22 studies evaluating nine physical-therapy approaches for Rett syndrome. The reported interventions often improved motor function, autonomy, behavior, communication, or quality of life, but the evidence was low and heterogeneous, supporting individualized multimodal physical therapy rather than preference for any single approach.
papers.why: This systematic review identifies multiple physical and behavioral rehabilitation approaches reported to benefit Rett syndrome patients and recommends individualized multimodal programs to preserve autonomy and improve quality of life.

papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of an oral solution of risperidone (an antipsychotic medication) versus placebo in the treatment of behavioral symptoms in children with Pervasive Developmental Disorders (PDD).

Currently, there are no treatments that change the course of the disease, and clinical care is largely focused on managing symptoms. papers.summary: ANAVEX2-73-RS-002 is a Phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled dose escalation safety, tolerability and efficacy study in patients 18 years and older with RTT using endpoints including multiple clinical and exploratory molecular and biochemical measures.

papers.summary: This is a phase 2 , open label, dose escalating study of Lovastatin in Rett syndrome.

papers.title: New Genes Involved in Molecular Etiology of Rett Syndrome Through DNA Microarray Comparative Genomic Hybridization
papers.summary:

CDKL5 and FOXG1 have been recently discovered being involved in other forms of RTT. However, at least 5% of typical forms and more other atypical forms are not linked to any of 3 genes known to be involved in the disease.

The purpose of this study is to identify new genes involved in molecular etiology of typical and atypical forms of RTT.

papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficacy of fenfluramine hydrochloride (HCl) versus placebo in study participants with Rett syndrome (RTT).

papers.summary: The aim of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of triheptanoin in participants with Rett syndrome using laboratory values, electrocardiogram, rate of adverse events (AE), and physical exam.This study also seeks to evaluate the efficacy of UX007 (triheptanoin) in improving overall seizure frequency and dystonia.

papers.summary:

A mouse experimental model of Rett syndrome created by genetic invalidation of the MECP2 gene is available. papers.summary: To investigate the safety and tolerability of long-term treatment with oral trofinetide in girls with Rett syndrome

papers.title: Trial of Dextromethorphan in Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: Increased brain glutamate and its N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors found in the brain of younger Rett syndrome (RTT) patients cause toxic damage to neurons (the brain's nerve cells), and contributing to EEG spikes. Dextromethorphan (DM) acts by blocking NMDA/glutamate receptors. This study is being done to determine if DM will prevent the harmful over-stimulation of the neurons thereby reducing EEG spike activity. papers.summary: The FENRTT2 study will investigate the efficacy and safety of a medicinal cannabis plant extract with extremely low THC (delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol), NTI164, on Rett syndrome (RTT) in a crossover design. RTT is a devastating rare genetic condition affecting females and involves debilitating physical and intellectual symptoms. NTI164 is an oil which has demonstrated efficacy in reducing symptoms in several paediatric neurological conditions, including RTT, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and paediatric acute-onset neuropsychicatric syndrome (PANS). papers.title: Esketamine for the Treatment of Rett Syndrome
papers.summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to learn about the efficacy and safety of Esketamine for treating children with Rett syndrome (RTT).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* whether Esketamine treatment is effective in improving symptom severity for RTT.
* whether Esketamine is safe in the treatment of RTT. Participants will receive a weekly intravenous infusion of Esketamine for five weeks and will be assessed for disease severity and drug safety.

papers.title: A Safety Study of NNZ-2566 in Patients With Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether NNZ-2566 is safe and well tolerated in the treatment of Rett Syndrome in adolescent and adult females.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of TSHA-102 in Pediatric Females With Rett Syndrome (REVEAL Pediatric Study)
papers.summary:
The REVEAL Pediatric Study is a multi-center, Phase 1/2 open-label, dose-escalation and dose-expansion study of TSHA-102, an investigational gene therapy, in pediatric females with Rett Syndrome.

The safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of two dose levels will be evaluated. The study duration is up to 6 years.

papers.title: Rett REVOLUTION Trial: An Exploratory Evaluation of the Safety and Efficacy of Vorinostat in Rett Syndrome
papers.summary:
The RETT REVOLUTION trial is a placebo-controlled, single-blinded, exploratory study with patients serving as their own control ("N of 1" trial design) where the safety and efficacy of vorinostat in the treatment of Rett syndrome will be evaluated. Each patient will be self-controlled in an adapted N-of-1 study design methodology by using a 4-week placebo baseline. Vorinostat dose escalation will occur every 8 weeks of daily dosing: placebo, 80mg/m2/day, 160mg/m2/day.

Key study objectives will include:

papers.summary: Pediatric movement disorders comprise of a large number of different neurological diseases including Rett syndrome (RTT) and Tourette syndrome. Probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum PS128 is a diet supplement that available for human consumption. papers.summary: The study will examine the potential efficacy and safety of two pre- and post-biotics on markers for gut inflammation and intestinal microbiota ecology in patients with Rett syndrome. Moreover, this trial will search for possible effects on epileptogenesis and quality of life.

papers.title: Treatment of Rett Syndrome With Recombinant Human IGF-1
papers.summary: Investigators are recruiting children for a clinical trial using the medication recombinant human IGF-1 (a.k.a. mecasermin or INCRELEX) to see if it improves the health of children with Rett syndrome (RTT). While IGF-1 is approved by the Food \& Drug Administration (FDA) for certain use in children, it is considered an investigational drug in this trial because it has not previously been used to treat RTT. Information from this study will help determine if IGF-1 effectively treats RTT but will not necessarily lead to FDA approval of IGF-1 as a treatment for RTT.

papers.title: Study of the Pathogenesis of Rett Syndrome
papers.summary:
OBJECTIVES: I. Extend current knowledge of the phenotype and natural history of Rett syndrome (RS).

II. Continue the search for a cytogenetic and/or DNA marker. III. Study the effects of cholinergic drugs based on preliminary evidence for reduced levels of brain acetylcholine, while continuing supportive care to modify seizures, respiratory abnormalities, and motor disturbances, and improve nutrition, behavior, and learning.

IV. Identify targets for future therapeutic interventions, e.g., growth factors, to influence neurologic recovery.

papers.title: The Role of Dietary Calcium for the Treatment of Osteopenia in Girls With Rett Syndrome

papers.title: Phase 2 Study of EPI-743 for Treatment of Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: Rett syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder that primarily affects female children. Rett syndrome is characterized by significant elevation in blood markers of oxidative stress. EPI-743 is a novel therapeutic with demonstrated efficacy and safety in the treatment of disorders characterized by oxidative stress. The purpose of this study is to examine the safety and efficacy of EPI-743 in a population of children with Rett syndrome.

papers.title: Study to Assess Safety and Efficacy of Fingolimod in Children With Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: The Trial Objective is to assess safety and efficacy of oral fingolimod (FTY720) in children older than 6 years with Rett Syndrome. So far there is no established treatment for children with Rett Syndrome. Therefore a positive result in terms of safety and first indications of efficacy would path the way to a phase II clinical study with more patients to further test the hypothesis that fingolimod treatment may slow down the regression of motor and language skills.

papers.title: Study of ANAVEX2-73 in Patients With Rett Syndrome
papers.summary:
Phase 2 safety, tolerability and efficacy study is designed as a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study.

7-week placebo-controlled study of ANAVEX2-73 oral solution for the treatment of patients with RTT 18 years or older. A voluntary option will be offered for all patients who meet the exposure criteria for ANAVEX2-73 to continue a 12-week open label extension.

papers.title: Assessing the Safety and Efficacy of Full-Spectrum Medicinal Cannabis Plant Extract 0.08% THC (NTI164) in the Treatment of Rett Syndrome (RTT)
papers.summary:
This 18-week open-label study examines the effectiveness of Full-Spectrum Medicinal Cannabis Plant Extract containing 0.08% THC (NTI164) in treating Rett syndrome (RTT) in children and young people. The study aims to determine the impact of NTI164 on RTT symptoms over a 16-week treatment period.

Participants will start with a daily dose of 5 mg/kg of NTI164, which will be gradually increased over four weeks until they reach either the maximum tolerated dose or 20 mg/kg per day. They will then maintain this dose for eight weeks. Following this treatment phase, the dosage will be reduced by 5 m

papers.title: Single-Dose AAV-MECP2 Safety/Tolerability and Efficacy in Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a serious neurodevelopmental disorder that has a significant impact on patients and their families. Patients suffer from severe social dysfunction and poor quality of life, and there is currently no effective treatment available. The MECP2 functional loss mutation is the clear pathogenic factor. In recent years, gene therapy has been applied in neuromuscular diseases such as SMA and has achieved good safety and effectiveness. Professor Qiu Zilong's self-developed AAV-MECP2 gene therapy product for RTT was found to significantly improve disease symptoms in RTT model mice,

papers.title: An Open Label, Exploratory Study to Investigate the Treatment Effect of Glatiramer Acetate on Girls Woth Rett Syndrome
papers.summary:
Primary Objective: To test the hypothesis that 6 months treatment with glatiramer acetate (GA) decreases epileptiform activity in young girls with Rett syndrome.

Primary Safety Objective:To evaluate the safety and tolerability of 6 months treatment with GA in these patients.

Secondary Objectives:

1. To test the hypothesis that 6 months treatment with glatiramer acetate (GA) improves respiratory dysfunction.
2. To evaluate the effect of GA treatment on general behaviour communication, hand stereotyping, feeding, sleep and other autonomic symptoms: gastrointestinal and cardiac.

papers.title: An Exploratory Trial of Ketamine for the Treatment of Rett Syndrome
papers.summary:
Rett Syndrome (RTT) is a complex disorder resulting from mutations in a gene encoding the MeCP2 protein. Currently, there are no methods to fix the abnormal gene, however, animal studies suggest that the symptoms of RTT can be treated.

Ketamine is a sedative or anesthetic, depending on the dose. The drug is approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and is commonly used in children and adults. Animal studies and case reports in humans suggest that ketamine may reduce the symptoms of Rett syndrome. The purpose of this study is to determine the safety and efficacy of ketamine for tre

papers.title: A Novel, Regulated Gene Therapy (NGN-401) Study for Females With Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: This study will evaluate the efficacy and safety profiles of the investigational gene therapy, NGN-401, in females with typical Rett syndrome.

papers.title: Study of Trofinetide for the Treatment of Girls and Women With Rett Syndrome (LAVENDER™)
papers.summary: To investigate the efficacy of treatment with oral trofinetide versus placebo in females with Rett syndrome

papers.title: A Safety Study of NNZ-2566 in Pediatric Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether NNZ-2566 is safe and well tolerated in the treatment of Rett syndrome in children and adolescents.

papers.title: ANAVEX2-73 Study in Pediatric Patients With Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: ANAVEX2-73-RS-003 is a Phase 2/3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled dose escalation safety, tolerability and efficacy study in patients 5-17 years of age with RTT using endpoints including multiple clinical and exploratory molecular and biochemical measures.

papers.title: Pharmacological Treatment of Rett Syndrome With Glatiramer Acetate (Copaxone)
papers.summary: A phase 2 open label trial to test a potential drug treatment for Rett syndrome, the leading known genetic cause of severe neurological impairment in girls. The drug, Copaxone (generic name - Glatiramer acetate) is medication FDA approved for the treatment of multiple sclerosis. Copaxone's high safety profile has been documented in large cohorts of patients for more than 12 years.

papers.title: Independent Studies of Dextromethorphan and of Donepezil Hydrochloride for Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a disorder in which the nervous system does not develop properly. RTT generally affects girls, but there are some boys who have been diagnosed with RTT. Symptoms of RTT include small brain size, poor language skills, repetitive hand movements, and seizures. This study will evaluate the effectiveness of two drugs in treating the symptoms of RTT.

papers.title: Repurposing Mirtazapine in Rett Syndrome
papers.summary: Rett Syndrome (RTT) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by an MECP2 gene mutation on the X chromosome, primarily affecting females. It causes progressive motor and cognitive decline, loss of speech, repetitive hand movements, breathing issues, seizures, and sleep problems. Given RTT's association with reduced monoamine levels, antidepressants like mirtazapine (MTZ) may help.Preclinical studies in MeCP2-mutant mice and early adult RTT trials showed that MTZ improved respiratory, motor, and neurological function, sleep, and mood, prompting this pediatric and young adult study. The Mirta

papers.summary:

The investigator plans to conduct 2-3 dose groups.
