papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Rett syndrome
An RNA editing strategy rescues gene duplication in a mouse model of MECP2 duplication syndrome and nonhuman primates.
papers.summary: The study developed an RNA-targeting hfCas13Y system to degrade excess MECP2 messenger RNA in models of MECP2 duplication syndrome. AAV delivery reduced MECP2 protein and dysregulated gene expression, improved behavioral deficits, and extended survival in transgenic mice; in nonhuman primates, a single injection produced widespread brain expression and 52.19% MECP2 knockdown.

papers.title: Targeted epigenetic repression by CRISPR/dSaCas9 suppresses pathogenic DUX4-fl expression in FSHD.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that a skeletal-muscle-specific CRISPR interference platform using dSaCas9 fused to the MeCP2 transcriptional repression domain can establish repressive chromatin and reduce pathogenic DUX4-fl expression and downstream target-gene expression in FSHD myocytes and an FSHD-like mouse model. The MeCP2-TRD construct showed minimal off-target transcriptional effects and is AAV-deliverable, providing an epigenetic repression strategy potentially transferable to disorders involving MECP2-regulated chromatin or gene expression, although no Rett syndrome experiments were performed.

papers.title: Gene therapy using an ortholog of human fragile X mental retardation protein partially rescues behavioral abnormalities and EEG activity.
papers.summary: In neonatal Fmr1-knockout rats and mice, AAV9 vectors driven by a mini-MeCP2 promoter and encoding rat Fmr1 isoform X3 or mouse Fmr1 isoform 7 produced widespread neuronal FMRP expression. The intervention partially corrected behavioral and EEG abnormalities in Fmr1-knockout rats, but did not correct abnormal gamma oscillations, had little effect on fear conditioning, and showed limited expression in parvalbumin interneurons and caudal brain regions.

papers.title: Hepatic stellate cell-specific miR-214 expression alleviates liver fibrosis without boosting steatosis and inflammation.
papers.summary: In an alcohol-associated liver fibrosis model and human LX-2 hepatic stellate cells, miR-214 overexpression reduced fibrogenic activity, and reporter experiments showed that it directly targets and suppresses MECP2. HSC-specific AAV8 delivery was more favorable than whole-liver delivery because it reduced fibrosis without the steatosis and inflammatory worsening observed with non-cell-specific expression, but the work was preclinical and did not test Rett syndrome.

papers.title: Comparison of neonatal systemic and intracerebroventricular AAV9 gene therapy delivery demonstrating improved behavioral and phenotypic outcomes in a mouse model of Niemann-Pick disease, type C1.
papers.summary: In Npc1-/- mice, earlier AAV9-hNPC1 gene therapy delivered systemically or intracerebroventricularly improved survival, disease phenotypes, motor function, and Purkinje-cell preservation compared with later systemic treatment. A truncated Mecp2-derived promoter performed no differently from the EF1α(s) promoter, while the paper additionally notes that an AAV9 clinical trial for Rett syndrome used intracerebroventricular dosing but reports no outcome data from that trial.

papers.title: Systemic neonatal AAV9 gene therapy delivery improves behavioral and phenotypic outcomes comparable to intracerebroventricular delivery in a mouse model of Niemann-Pick disease, type C1
papers.summary: This preprint reports that neonatal systemic AAV9 delivery of an NPC1 gene construct improves survival, slows disease progression, and produces phenotypic and Purkinje cell rescue in Npc1-deficient mice, comparable to intracerebroventricular delivery. A truncated Mecp2-derived promoter performed similarly to a ubiquitous EF1α-derived promoter, but the study did not demonstrate that the construct targets or modifies MECP2 itself.

papers.title: Inhibition of KDM1A activity restores adult neurogenesis and improves hippocampal memory in a mouse model of Kabuki syndrome.
papers.summary: In Kmt2d+/βGeo mice modeling Kabuki syndrome, oral TAK-418 inhibition of KDM1A partially restored H3K4 methylation, chromatin-associated gene-expression abnormalities, adult hippocampal neurogenesis, and hippocampal learning and memory. The study provides preclinical evidence that targeted modulation of chromatin remodeling can ameliorate KMT2D-related neurological phenotypes, although effects were incomplete in some molecular measures and translation to humans is unknown.

papers.title: Rescue of deficits by Brwd1 copy number restoration in the Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome.
papers.summary: In Down syndrome models, increased BRWD1 expression causes BAF chromatin-remodeling mistargeting, aberrant chromatin accessibility, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive deficits. Genetic Brwd1 copy-number restoration partially rescues these molecular and behavioral abnormalities, while acute BRWD1 overexpression is sufficient to induce neuronal and cognitive defects.

papers.title: Pantothenate and L-Carnitine Supplementation Improves Pathological Alterations in Cellular Models of KAT6A Syndrome.
papers.summary: In patient-derived fibroblasts carrying pathogenic KAT6A variants, the study shows reduced KAT6A expression, histone H3 hypoacetylation, altered gene-expression patterns, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired survival under nutritional stress. Pantothenate and L-carnitine increased histone acetylation, restored expression of multiple affected proteins and transcriptional patterns, improved mitochondrial bioenergetics, and rescued mutant-cell survival in vitro.

papers.title: Neuronal network dysfunction in a human model for Kleefstra syndrome mediated by enhanced NMDAR signaling
papers.summary: The paper links EHMT1 deficiency in Kleefstra syndrome to reduced repressive H3K9me2 at the GRIN1 promoter, increased NMDAR signaling, and abnormal neuronal-network activity in human iPSC-derived neurons and mice. Pharmacological NMDAR inhibition rescued the patient-derived neuronal-network phenotypes, although the reported intervention acts downstream of the epigenetic defect rather than directly on chromatin remodeling.

papers.title: Abnormal Chromatin Remodeling Caused by ARID1A Deletion Leads to Malformation of the Dentate Gyrus
papers.summary: Arid1a deletion in the mouse forebrain disrupts chromatin remodeling, reduces neural stem/progenitor-cell proliferation and neuronal differentiation, increases apoptosis, and leads to a smaller hippocampus. Prox1 overexpression rescues the proliferation and differentiation defects, while ARID1A-dependent regulation of Prox1 through altered histone modifications suggests a mechanism potentially relevant to intellectual disability and Coffin–Siris syndrome.

papers.title: Pantothenate and L-carnitine Supplementation Corrects Pathological Alterations in Cellular Models of KAT6A Syndrome
papers.summary: This preprint reports that pantothenate and L-carnitine correct several pathological alterations in patient-derived fibroblasts carrying KAT6A mutations. The treatments increased histone acetylation, corrected protein and transcriptomic expression patterns, and improved cellular bioenergetics in KAT6A syndrome cellular models.

papers.title: Targeting pancreatic cancer by TAK-981: a SUMOylation inhibitor that activates the immune system and blocks cancer cell cycle progression in a preclinical model.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the SUMO E1 inhibitor TAK-981 decreases SUMOylation in pancreatic cancer cells, causing cell-cycle arrest, mitotic failure, and chromosomal segregation defects while reducing tumour growth in KPC3 syngeneic mice. TAK-981 also alters immune-cell populations and activates interferon-associated STAT1 signalling, but it does not mention or test MeCP2 or MeCP2 small ubiquitin-like modifier 1 modification.

papers.title: Circular RNA-encoded oncogenic PIAS1 variant blocks immunogenic ferroptosis by modulating the balance between SUMOylation and phosphorylation of STAT1.
papers.summary: In melanoma, circPIAS1 encodes the 108-amino-acid peptide circPIAS1-108aa, which recruits Ranbp2 to increase STAT1 SUMOylation at Lys703 and Glu705, thereby reducing STAT1 phosphorylation at Tyr701 and suppressing IFNγ-induced immunogenic ferroptosis. CircPIAS1 knockdown restored ferroptosis and enhanced PD-1-inhibitor activity in melanoma models, but the paper did not investigate MeCP2 small ubiquitin-like modifier 1 modification or establish transfer to Rett syndrome.

papers.title: Co-delivery of camptothecin and MiR-145 by lipid nanoparticles for MRI-visible targeted therapy of hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.summary: In hepatocellular carcinoma models, lactobionic acid-modified lipid nanoparticles co-delivering camptothecin and miR-145 suppressed tumor growth, prolonged survival, and promoted apoptosis. Mechanistically, miR-145 reduced SENP1, increased HK2 SUMOylation, disrupted HK2–VDAC1 binding, decreased glycolysis, and sensitized cancer cells to camptothecin; however, the paper did not examine MeCP2 small ubiquitin-like modifier 1 modification or Rett syndrome.

papers.title: SUMOylation of AnxA6 facilitates EGFR-PKCα complex formation to suppress epithelial cancer growth.
papers.summary: The paper does not study MeCP2 or MeCP2 small ubiquitin-like modifier 1 modification; it instead provides an analogous SUMOylation system in which AnxA6 SUMO1 conjugation at K299 promotes EGFR–PKCα complex formation and suppresses EGFR–ERK signaling, cancer-cell growth, migration, xenograft growth, and gefitinib resistance. Chemical SUMOylation inhibitors, SUMO1 site mutagenesis, immunoprecipitation, and LC–MS/MS provide experimentally supported intervention and measurement strategies that could be transferred to a MeCP2 SUMOylation system, but transfer to Rett syndrome remains untested.

papers.title: miR-382-3p downregulation contributes to the carcinogenesis of lung adenocarcinoma by promoting AKT SUMOylation and phosphorylation.
papers.summary: The study shows that miR-382-3p downregulation increases SAE1 expression, promotes AKT SUMOylation and phosphorylation, and contributes to lung adenocarcinoma growth and survival. miR-382-3p overexpression restrained xenograft growth, while SAE1 knockdown partially reversed the proliferative and anti-apoptotic effects of miR-382-3p inhibition; the paper does not examine MeCP2 or Rett syndrome.

papers.title: Identifying SUMOylation-related genes in liver fibrosis with bioinformatics and experimental models for diagnostic insights.
papers.summary: This paper identifies SUMOylation-related gene-expression changes associated with liver fibrosis and validates selected changes in a CCl₄-induced mouse model. It proposes NR3C2, PCNA, THRB, CDKN2A, DNMT1, MDM2, SMC6, and RXRA as diagnostic biomarkers, but it does not investigate MECP2, MeCP2 small ubiquitin-like modifier 1 modification, or an intervention that directly modifies MeCP2.

papers.title: Comparing Automated Morphology Quantification Software on Dendrites of Uninjured and Injured Drosophila Neurons.
papers.summary: The study benchmarks automated neuron-tracing pipelines for measuring dendritic arborization in uninjured and laser-injured Drosophila class IV dendritic arborization neurons. Imaris best reproduced branch-count and dendrite-length conclusions and was faster than manual tracing, but all tested pipelines had accuracy limitations and none accurately quantified total dendrite length after manual correction.

papers.title: Automated analysis of neuronal morphology, synapse number and synaptic recruitment.
papers.summary: The paper develops an automated image-analysis routine using steerable filters and deconvolutions to quantify dendrite morphology, synapse number, synapse size, synaptic vesicle density, and protein accumulation in immunofluorescence images. The method is intended to reduce labor, human bias, and analysis time while supporting batch and high-throughput analysis; no disease, intervention, or patient/model outcome is evaluated.

papers.title: Multiscale Assay of Unlabeled Neurite Dynamics Using Phase Imaging with Computational Specificity.
papers.summary: The paper introduces phase imaging with computational specificity (PICS), a label-free, deep-learning-assisted assay that combines quantitative phase imaging with inferred Tau/MAP2 staining to monitor live neuronal growth, dendritic arborization, and intracellular transport. Applied to primary hippocampal cultures, PICS tracked arborization and compartment-specific dry-mass dynamics across hundreds of fields and thousands of neurons without the fixation required for antibody-based dendritic markers.

papers.title: An Optimized and Detailed Step-by-Step Protocol for the Analysis of Neuronal Morphology in Golgi-Stained Fetal Sheep Brain.
papers.summary: The paper provides a reproducible workflow for quantifying dendritic and other neuronal morphology in Golgi-stained fetal sheep brain using the FD Rapid GolgiStain kit and Imaris software. Applied to hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons, the workflow measures dendritic length, branching, branch order, Sholl intersections, and dendritic-spine features relevant to assessing dendritic arborization.

papers.title: NeurphologyJ: an automatic neuronal morphology quantification method and its application in pharmacological discovery.
papers.summary: The paper develops and validates NeurphologyJ, an ImageJ-based automated method for quantifying neuronal morphology from fluorescence images, including soma number, neurite length, attachment points, and ending points. In differentiated P19 cells and primary mouse hippocampal neurons, the method accurately measured neurite morphology and detected nocodazole-induced neurite retraction, with a calculated IC50 of 42 ng/mL.

papers.title: Rapid reconstruction of 3D neuronal morphology from light microscopy images with augmented rayburst sampling.
papers.summary: The paper presents flNeuronTool, a free interactive system that uses augmented rayburst sampling to rapidly reconstruct three-dimensional neuronal morphology, including dendritic trees and local neural circuits. Validation on synthetic images, DIADEM datasets, and mouse-brain MOST images showed generally high reconstruction accuracy, with poor performance on beaded or approximately one-voxel-wide dendrites.

papers.title: Danthron Attenuates Intestinal Inflammation by Modulating Oxidative Stress via the EGFR-PI3K-AKT and Nrf2-HO-1 Pathways.
papers.summary: In inflammatory bowel disease models, Danthron reduced reactive oxygen species and mitochondrial superoxide, partially restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and activated the Nrf2–HO-1 antioxidant program. These findings identify Danthron and the mitochondrial readouts MitoSOX and JC-10 as transferable experimental solutions for testing mitochondrial dysfunction, but no effects in Rett syndrome were investigated.

papers.title: N-Acetylglucosamine Selectively Attenuates Neuroinflammation in a Mouse Model of Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
papers.summary: In the Coq9 R239X mouse model of fatal mitochondrial encephalopathy, oral N-acetylglucosamine reduced astrocyte and microglial activation and suppressed NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammatory signaling, with partial improvement in motor coordination and early survival. It did not restore myelin protein expression, correct body-weight deficit, prolong maximum lifespan, or halt disease progression, indicating that targeting downstream neuroinflammation can provide limited functional benefit without repairing mitochondrial pathology.

papers.title: Optimization of M1 macrophage targeting using a glucosylated albumin nanoplatform for ROS scavenging and mitochondrial rescue in acute kidney injury.
papers.summary: In ischemia–reperfusion-induced acute kidney injury, the glucosylated albumin nanoplatform Glc6-AD11-Alb targets inflammatory M1 macrophages and directly protects stressed renal tubular epithelial cells from oxidative and hypoxic injury. The intervention reduced ROS and apoptosis, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, respiration, ATP-linked oxidative phosphorylation, and ultrastructure, improved renal function and regeneration in vivo, and therefore provides an experimentally supported strategy for targeting mitochondrial dysfunction in a non-neural disease.

papers.title: Nicotinamide riboside prevents mitochondrial dysfunction in nemaline myopathy type 6.
papers.summary: In a homozygous Kbtbd13R408C knock-in mouse model of nemaline myopathy type 6, chronic nicotinamide riboside treatment improved mitochondrial ultrastructure and preserved oxidative phosphorylation and substrate-linked respiration. The treatment did not prevent core formation or mitochondrial biogenesis, and the study lacked a placebo control and in vivo functional outcome testing.

papers.title: UA-30 ameliorates motor deficits through RalA-mediated mitophagy in ALS mice.
papers.summary: In SOD1G93A mouse and cellular models of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, the orally active RalA inhibitor UA-30 improved motor function, preserved motor neurons, and partially extended survival. Its mechanistic effects included stabilizing FOXO3a, increasing PINK1/Parkin-associated mitophagy, and ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction; constitutively active RalA or Mdivi-1 co-treatment blocked these benefits.

papers.title: β-Hydroxybutyrate-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress in BMSCs are ameliorated by mitophagy activation.
papers.summary: In bovine muscle satellite cells and murine C2C12 myoblasts, elevated β-Hydroxybutyrate induced oxidative stress, impaired mitochondrial structure and function, and suppressed mitophagy. Pharmacologic mitophagy inhibition with 3-methyladenine worsened injury, whereas CCCP-mediated activation reduced ROS and improved antioxidant status, but both agents lack mitophagy specificity and the experiments provide only in-vitro cellular proof of concept.

unread.title: Multidisciplinary Management of Rett Syndrome: Twenty Years' Experience.
unread.why: A 20-year, 103-patient Rett syndrome cohort provides actionable multidisciplinary management principles and longitudinal measures of disease progression, comorbidities, function, and survival.

unread.title: Novel FOXG1 mutations in Chinese patients with Rett syndrome or Rett-like mental retardation.
unread.why: Testing 451 patients identified FOXG1 variants in Rett and Rett-like intellectual disability and supports FOXG1 testing, particularly in congenital cases with corpus callosum hypoplasia.

unread.title: Monogenic disorders that mimic the phenotype of Rett syndrome.
unread.why: Whole-exome sequencing in seven MECP2-negative, Rett-like patients identified six alternative genetic diagnoses and provides a practical differential-diagnostic strategy.

unread.title: Analysis of FOXG1 Is Highly Recommended in Male and Female Patients with Rett Syndrome.
unread.why: Direct FOXG1 screening of a Rett spectrum cohort identified pathogenic variants and provides a concrete testing strategy for cases without established Rett-syndrome gene diagnoses.

unread.title: Translational reading frame determines the pathogenicity of C-terminal frameshift deletions in MeCP2: an alternative therapeutic approach.
unread.why: The study identifies a structure-based rule distinguishing pathogenic MECP2 frameshifts and demonstrates base-editor correction with phenotypic rescue in cells and a Rett mouse model.

unread.title: MECP2 MBD-ID Module: A Unified DNA/RNA Binding Interface Disrupted in Rett Syndrome.
unread.why: The work experimentally defines the disease-relevant MECP2 MBD-ID binding interface and tests a MiniGene intervention against Rett-associated binding defects.

unread.title: RettBASE: Rett syndrome database update.
unread.why: RettBASE is an established disease-specific resource containing curated variants and phenotype-genotype information for Rett syndrome and related phenotypes.

unread.title: Respiratory and sleep disorders in female children with atypical Rett syndrome caused by mutations in the CDKL5 gene.
unread.why: Validated sleep assessment and polysomnography identified clinically important respiratory and sleep abnormalities in CDKL5-associated atypical Rett syndrome and can be reused for similar patients.

unread.title: Phenotypes in adult patients with Rett syndrome: results of a 13-year experience and insights into healthcare transition.
unread.why: The study delineates adult Rett syndrome manifestations and supports a dedicated multidisciplinary transition program and age-specific clinical monitoring.

unread.title: MECP2 Dysfunction in Rett Syndrome: Molecular Mechanisms, Multisystem Pathology, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
unread.why: This review directly summarizes molecular and therapeutic strategies for MECP2 dysfunction in Rett syndrome, including gene therapy and other intervention platforms.

unread.title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlation and Therapeutic Amenability in a Cohort of Rett Syndrome Patients: A Single-Center Study.
unread.why: The cohort provides Rett-specific clinical and genetic data supporting Trofinetide eligibility, treatment planning, and outcome tracking across MECP2 variants.

unread.title: Key clinical features to identify girls with CDKL5 mutations.
unread.why: The study establishes a targeted CDKL5 screening strategy and clinical criteria for identifying Rett-like disease in girls with early seizures and severe hypotonia.

unread.title: Variant of Rett syndrome and CDKL5 gene: clinical and autonomic description of 10 cases.
unread.why: This study applies an existing autonomic assessment instrument to ten patients with CDKL5-related atypical Rett syndrome and identifies measurable cardiorespiratory phenotypes.

unread.title: Somatic mosaicism of a CDKL5 mutation identified by next-generation sequencing.
unread.why: The case provides direct evidence that a targeted next-generation sequencing assay can identify causal and potentially contributory variants in a patient with an atypical Rett phenotype.

unread.title: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number in Rett Syndrome Caused by Methyl-CpG-Binding Protein-2 Variants.
unread.why: The study establishes increased peripheral-blood mtDNA copy number in 142 MECP2-variant Rett patients as a candidate mitochondrial biomarker and validates a concrete qPCR assay.

unread.title: Transduction of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells by an <i>MECP2</i> lentiviral vector improves Rett syndrome phenotypes.
unread.why: The study provides proof-of-concept transplantation data showing brain MeCP2 expression and improvement of motor phenotypes after delivering an MECP2 vector in human hematopoietic cells to Rett mice.

unread.title: Evaluation Tools Developed for Rett Syndrome.
unread.why: The paper consolidates Rett syndrome-specific validated tools for measuring severity, motor function, hand use, mobility, activity, behavior, and fear of movement.

unread.title: Preclinical Milestones in MECP2 Gene Transfer for Treating Rett Syndrome.
unread.why: This review documents tested preclinical MECP2 gene-transfer designs and regulatory strategies developed specifically to treat Rett syndrome while controlling MeCP2 dose toxicity.

unread.title: miR126-mediated alteration of vascular integrity in Rett syndrome.
unread.why: Patient-derived iPSC endothelial cells and a Rett microvascular network model reveal a rescuable miR-126-3p-associated vascular-barrier defect.

unread.title: Evaluation of Novel Enhancer Compounds in Gentamicin-Mediated Readthrough of Nonsense Mutations in Rett Syndrome.
unread.why: The study experimentally demonstrates that CDX readthrough enhancers potentiate gentamicin to restore full-length MeCP2 in common MECP2 nonsense-mutant systems and reduce the gentamicin dose needed.

unread.title: The Heart of Rett Syndrome: A Quantitative Analysis of Cardiac Repolarization.
unread.why: Quantitative ECG analysis identifies genotype-associated QTc and T-wave abnormalities in Rett syndrome and supports their potential use in monitoring and mortality-risk assessment.

unread.title: Non-canonical C-terminal variant of MeCP2 R344W exhibits enhanced degradation rate.
unread.why: Patient-variant characterization provides experimentally tested assays for MeCP2 degradation, corepressor interaction, and localization while identifying protein stability as a candidate therapeutic target.

unread.title: Top Caregiver Concerns in Rett syndrome and related disorders: data from the US Natural History Study.
unread.why: This natural-history study provides an Rett syndrome cohort and prioritizes communication, seizures, walking/balance, hand use, and constipation for clinical-trial outcome planning.

unread.title: miR126-mediated impaired vascular integrity in Rett syndrome
unread.why: The study develops patient-derived Rett microvascular models and experimentally rescues abnormal vascular permeability by reducing miR-126-3p.

unread.title: Safety and effectiveness of diazepam nasal spray in patients with Rett syndrome and seizure clusters: <i>post hoc</i> analyses from a long-term safety study and survey of severity and burden.
unread.why: An open-label Rett cohort provides direct safety and effectiveness data for diazepam nasal spray as a rescue treatment for seizure clusters.

unread.title: Heat shock factor 1 signaling: A novel pathway implicated in Rett syndrome pathophysiology.
unread.why: Human transcriptomic validation and mouse experiments identify HSF1 signaling as pathogenic and show that its inhibition improves Rett-like phenotypes.

unread.title: Modulating alternative splicing of <i>MECP2</i> is a potential therapeutic strategy for Rett syndrome.
unread.why: The study demonstrates exon-2-skipping-mediated MECP2 upregulation and phenotypic or transcriptomic rescue in Rett cell models and mice.

unread.title: Neurogenic colonic motility patterns and gut transit disrupted in a mouse model of Rett Syndrome
unread.why: The study establishes Rett gastrointestinal phenotypes, identifies their neuronal source, and shows that muscarinic M1 receptor modulation alters abnormal colonic contractions.

unread.title: Rett syndrome lifespan extension in mice via AI-guided ADAR editing
unread.why: The study demonstrates targeted correction of an MECP2 nonsense mutation by ADAR editing with MeCP2 restoration, phenotypic improvement, and lifespan extension in Rett models.

unread.title: MeCP2 is Necessary in Cerebellar Purkinje Cells for Precise Network Dynamics During Associative Motor Learning
unread.why: The study establishes a Rett-relevant Purkinje-cell model and directly maps MECP2 loss to cerebellar network activity and motor-learning phenotypes.

unread.title: MECP2 -mutant marmosets exhibit primate-specific phenotypes of Rett syndrome
unread.why: This paper creates a gene-engineered primate model of Rett syndrome and identifies conserved cellular and molecular targets relevant to therapeutic development.

unread.title: Structures of MeCP2 bound to nucleosomes reveal distinct mechanisms of Rett syndrome mutations
unread.why: It provides variant-resolved structural and biochemical assays that directly characterize how MECP2 mutations impair nucleosome binding and chromatin targeting in Rett syndrome.

unread.title: Early postnatal DNA methylation dynamics define neuronal subtypes and are disrupted by MECP2 loss
unread.why: The study supplies a reusable single-cell methylation atlas and assays that identify subtype-specific epigenetic signatures disrupted by MECP2 loss in Rett syndrome.

unread.title: Molecular and Functional Dysregulations in Novel, Rett Syndrome Patient-Derived Cerebral Organoids
unread.why: The paper establishes a scalable patient-derived organoid model and demonstrates its use for testing AAV9-mediated therapeutic delivery in Rett syndrome.

unread.title: Mecp2 deficiency impairs microscale cortical network topology and dynamics in a Rett syndrome mouse model
unread.why: The study validates an in vitro Rett syndrome cortical-network assay with quantitative connectivity outcomes that could screen restorative therapies.

unread.title: Mecp2 deficiency induces dysphagia in a preclinical model of Rett Syndrome
unread.why: This work establishes a preclinical Rett syndrome model and objective neurophysiological endpoints for studying dysphagia and aspiration-related respiratory dysfunction.

unread.title: MeCP2 NID interaction with RNA: Implications for Rett Syndrome-Relevant Protein Regulation
unread.why: The paper develops assays for a noncanonical MeCP2 RNA interaction that regulates NCoR binding and may provide a targetable Rett syndrome mechanism.

unread.title: IGF1 peptide targets Rett Syndrome astrocytes to degrade IGF binding protein, rescue synaptogenesis and restore mitochondrial function
unread.why: The study tests an IGF1-derived peptide that degrades elevated astrocytic IGFBP2 and restores synaptic and mitochondrial function in Rett syndrome models.

unread.title: Impaired astrocyte-to-neuron cholesterol trafficking drives synaptic dysfunction in Rett syndrome
unread.why: The paper demonstrates that restoring astrocyte-to-neuron cholesterol availability rescues synaptic and neuronal defects caused by Mecp2 loss in Rett syndrome models.

unread.title: An automated machine vision-based index for Rett Syndrome provides a generalizable framework for modeling rare disease therapeutics
unread.why: This study develops and validates a high-resolution automated outcome measure that detects Rett severity and partial therapeutic rescue more sensitively than the Bird score.

unread.title: Clinical experience using trofinetide in Rett syndrome and related MECP2 diagnosis at the children's hospital of Philadelphia post approval.
unread.why: This real-world study reports clinical use of FDA-approved trofinetide in 55 people with Rett or MECP2-related neurodevelopmental disorder, including symptom outcomes and adverse events.

unread.title: Rett syndrome: MECP2 biology, multisystem pathophysiology, and the evolving therapeutic landscape.
unread.why: This Rett-focused review summarizes solutions and preclinical data showing phenotypic improvement after MECP2 reactivation in rodents, iPSC-derived neurons, and organoids, alongside clinical therapies and unmet biomarker needs.

unread.title: ANAVEX®2-73 (blarcamesine), a Sigma-1 receptor agonist, ameliorates neurologic impairments in a mouse model of Rett syndrome.
unread.why: Blarcamesine was directly administered to a MeCP2-deficient mouse model and improved multiple motor, sensory, autonomic, and respiratory phenotypes relevant to Rett syndrome.

unread.title: Comparison of Core Features in Four Developmental Encephalopathies in the Rett Natural History Study.
unread.why: This large natural-history study provides a directly usable clinical dataset and comparative outcome measures across Rett syndrome and related developmental encephalopathies.

unread.title: Trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome: Results from the open-label extension LILAC study.
unread.why: The 40-week LILAC extension directly evaluated long-term trofinetide treatment and safety in 154 females with Rett syndrome using behavioral and global-improvement endpoints.

unread.title: A Potential Life-Threatening Reaction to Glatiramer Acetate in Rett Syndrome.
unread.why: An open-label Rett syndrome trial directly tested glatiramer acetate and identified life-threatening immediate post-injection reactions that materially inform its safety assessment.

unread.title: Novel mutations in cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) gene in Indian cases of Rett syndrome.
unread.why: The study tested an actionable CDKL5 screening and in-silico analysis workflow in MECP2-negative atypical Rett syndrome and identified potentially deleterious variants.

unread.title: Novel mutation in forkhead box G1 (FOXG1) gene in an Indian patient with Rett syndrome.
unread.why: FOXG1 molecular testing in MECP2/CDKL5-negative Rett syndrome identified a potentially pathogenic frameshift variant and supports a differential diagnostic workflow.

unread.title: Real-world benefits and tolerability of trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome: The LOTUS study.
unread.why: The LOTUS study provides real-world treatment outcomes and tolerability data for trofinetide in Rett syndrome using structured behavioral, quality-of-life, and gastrointestinal measures.

unread.title: Identification of a de novo mutation of the FOXG1 gene and comprehensive analysis for molecular factors in Chinese FOXG1-related encephalopathies.
unread.why: The study supplies diagnostic methods and genetic evidence for FOXG1-related encephalopathy, a disorder overlapping congenital Rett syndrome, and identifies regulatory mechanisms that may affect MECP2 and CDKL5.

unread.title: Associations Among Diurnal Salivary Cortisol Patterns, Medication Use, and Behavioral Phenotype Features in a Community Sample of Rett Syndrome.
unread.why: The study shows that diurnal salivary cortisol patterns can be measured in Rett syndrome and associated with mutation severity, anticonvulsant use, and bruxism.

unread.title: Is highly purified cannabidiol a treatment opportunity for drug-resistant epilepsy in subjects with typical Rett syndrome and CDKL5 deficiency disorder?
unread.why: This observational cohort provides patient data on adjunctive cannabidiol for drug-resistant epilepsy in genetically confirmed Rett syndrome and CDKL5 deficiency disorder.

unread.title: Clapping-surpressed focal spikes in EEG may be unique for the patients with rett syndrome : a case report.
unread.why: The report identifies a reproducible EEG signature that suppresses with hand-clapping stereotypies and may assist recognition or diagnosis of Rett syndrome.

unread.title: [Case of Rett syndrome monitored with BIS and neuromuscular monitor during total intravenous anesthesia].
unread.why: The case provides a tested perioperative monitoring and anesthesia-management approach for a child with Rett syndrome.

unread.title: Evidence of neuronal DNA damage in the brains of patients with Rett syndrome.
unread.why: The study develops single-neuron transcriptional profiling in patient brains, validates a MECP2-null rat model, and identifies disease-associated molecular signatures.

unread.title: Challenges in the Dental Management of Rett Syndrome under General Anesthesia: A Rare Disease.
unread.why: The report provides a concrete dental rehabilitation workflow for a patient with Rett syndrome under general anesthesia.

unread.title: Safety Profiles of Trofinetide in Pediatric Rett Syndrome Population: A Real-World Postmarketing Pharmacovigilance Analysis.
unread.why: This study provides real-world safety data and pharmacovigilance methods for the approved Rett syndrome drug trofinetide.

unread.title: Study of trofinetide in Rett syndrome: Lessons from an approved drug for a severe neurodevelopmental disorder.
unread.why: The paper directly studies an approved treatment for Rett syndrome, although the abstract does not provide specific study results.

unread.title: Real-world benefits and tolerability of trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome: The LOTUS study.
unread.why: The LOTUS study directly evaluates an existing trofinetide treatment for Rett syndrome, although no abstract is available for more detailed appraisal.

unread.title: A model for neural development and treatment of Rett syndrome using human induced pluripotent stem cells.
unread.why: This study develops a patient-derived iPSC neuronal model and uses it to test drug rescue of synaptic defects in Rett syndrome.

unread.title: Methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) mutation type is associated with disease severity in Rett syndrome.
unread.why: This large longitudinal Rett syndrome cohort identifies mutation-dependent severity and clinically usable predictors such as ambulation, hand use, and stereotypy onset.

unread.title: Long-read sequence analysis of the MECP2 gene in Rett syndrome patients: correlation of disease severity with mutation type and location.
unread.why: This study establishes a sequencing method for detecting and characterizing MECP2 mutations and links mutation class to Rett syndrome severity.

unread.title: MeCP2 mutations in children with and without the phenotype of Rett syndrome.
unread.why: The study provides a molecular testing workflow and clinical correlates of severity for classic and atypical Rett syndrome.

unread.title: CDKL5, a protein associated with rett syndrome, regulates neuronal morphogenesis via Rac1 signaling.
unread.why: The study provides mechanistic neuronal models and experimentally demonstrates Rac1-mediated rescue of dendrite defects caused by CDKL5 loss, a pathway relevant to Rett-associated neurodevelopmental phenotypes.

unread.title: Epilepsy in Rett syndrome, and CDKL5- and FOXG1-gene-related encephalopathies.
unread.why: The review consolidates clinically used diagnostic and outcome characteristics that distinguish typical Rett syndrome from CDKL5- and FOXG1-related encephalopathies.

unread.title: The array of clinical phenotypes of males with mutations in Methyl-CpG binding protein 2.
unread.why: Using a disease-specific natural-history database and standardized clinical review, the study defines the MECP2-associated male phenotype and supports improved genomic diagnosis.

unread.title: Mutational spectrum of CDKL5 in early-onset encephalopathies: a study of a large collection of French patients and review of the literature.
unread.why: The study directly validates CDKL5 sequencing and MLPA in patients with early-onset seizures and atypical Rett syndrome features.

unread.title: Mutations in epilepsy and intellectual disability genes in patients with features of Rett syndrome.
unread.why: Exome sequencing identified causal variants in patients with Rett-like phenotypes after negative MECP2 testing and supports an expanded differential diagnosis.

unread.title: Mutation spectrum in patients with Rett syndrome in the German population: Evidence of hot spot regions.
unread.why: Direct sequencing of 125 Rett syndrome cases established a high diagnostic yield and identified recurrent MECP2 mutation regions suitable for testing and interpretation.

unread.title: Rett syndrome: North American database.
unread.why: The 1,928-participant database is a substantial Rett syndrome biobank and research resource containing diagnosis, mutation, and prevalence data.

unread.title: Updating the profile of C-terminal MECP2 deletions in Rett syndrome.
unread.why: The pooled international cohort establishes genotype-stratified severity and growth outcomes for MECP2 C-terminal deletions using reusable clinical rating scales.

unread.title: Spectrum and distribution of MECP2 mutations in 424 Rett syndrome patients: a molecular update.
unread.why: Large-scale testing of 424 people with Rett syndrome established a diagnostic strategy that combines sequence-variant detection with quantitative analysis for MECP2 rearrangements.

unread.title: Imbalance of excitatory/inhibitory synaptic protein expression in iPSC-derived neurons from FOXG1(+/-) patients and in foxg1(+/-) mice.
unread.why: The paper provides patient-derived neurons and a mouse model that reproduce an excitatory/inhibitory synaptic imbalance relevant to Rett syndrome.

unread.title: Xp22.3 genomic deletions involving the CDKL5 gene in girls with early onset epileptic encephalopathy.
unread.why: The study identifies a substantial diagnostic yield in girls with CDKL5-related Rett-like encephalopathy and provides a combined sequence and copy-number testing strategy.

unread.title: Rett syndrome in adolescent and adult females: clinical and molecular genetic findings.
unread.why: The study supplies molecular diagnostic methods and clinically useful genotype-phenotype profiles for adolescent and adult Rett syndrome.

unread.title: MECP2 gene analysis in classical Rett syndrome and in patients with Rett-like features.
unread.why: MECP2 sequence analysis achieved a very high diagnostic yield in classical Rett syndrome and was also applied to preserved-speech and Rett-like cases.

unread.title: Methyl-CpG binding protein 2 gene (MECP2) variations in Japanese patients with Rett syndrome: pathological mutations and polymorphisms.
unread.why: Testing of 219 Japanese patients produced a disease-specific mutation spectrum and clinically relevant guidance for distinguishing pathogenic MECP2 variants from population polymorphisms.

unread.title: Trofinetide: First Approval.
unread.why: This review reports the development and first approval of trofinetide for Rett syndrome in adults and children aged 2 years and older.

unread.title: MECP2 and CDKL5 gene mutation analysis in Chinese patients with Rett syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly evaluates mutation-screening performance in 121 unrelated Chinese patients with classic or atypical Rett syndrome and reports diagnostic detection rates.

unread.title: MECP2 mutant allele in a boy with Rett syndrome and his unaffected heterozygous mother.
unread.why: The report provides direct evidence for testing affected children and their mothers for MECP2 mutations and for assessing skewed X inactivation in clinically unaffected carriers.
